idea-plugin.name: Honey Style
idea-plugin.description:
Shows a color swatch next to honey-style theme color paths in JavaScript and TypeScript.

The palette is read from the project's own theme sources, so nothing is hardcoded: any colors or palette object literal is flattened into dotted paths.

Recognised forms:

  • colors.primary.royalBlue and theme.colors.neutral.fogGrey
  • resolveColor('primary.royalBlue', 0.25) - alpha included in the swatch
  • honey-layout color props, e.g. $backgroundColor="accent.mediumGold"
  • bare paths inside styled/css template literals, e.g. border-color: secondary.mediumGreen;

Cmd/Ctrl+Click on a path jumps to the declaration that holds the value, e.g. royalBlue: '#318BFA' in the theme file.

Completion of color paths shows the actual color as the item icon, in resolveColor('...') arguments and after a palette group such as colors.primary..

Honey at-rules are completed inside styled/css template literals - @honey-media, @honey-stack, @honey-inline, @honey-center, @honey-if, @honey-ellipsis and @honey-absolute-fill - along with their parameters. Breakpoint names for @honey-media are read from the project's theme.breakpoints.

The gutter color picker snaps to the nearest token in the palette instead of writing a raw hex value, since only theme tokens are valid in these positions.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.4.0

  • Only real honey color paths are offered. A path is exactly group.name - resolveColor reads two parts of the split - so deeper ones such as button.accent.filled.color are gone, and only a colors property of a theme object counts as a palette. The deprecated standalone colors / colors2 objects are reached through theme.mg and never resolve in a honey position.
  • All 148 CSS named colors are recognised. The previous list held 42, so names like royalblue and rebeccapurple were silently ignored.
  • Extra color names can be configured in Settings > Tools > Honey Style, one name = value per line. They may also redefine a standard name.
  • The color props are configurable in the same place. They default to honey-layout's list, and the $ prefix is optional.
  • CSS color names offered by TypeScript in a color prop or resolveColor('...') now carry a swatch and hex too, not just theme paths.
  • Completion is grouped: theme tokens first, then CSS color names, then everything else TypeScript offers - inherit, unset, and the 38 deprecated CSS system colors such as Background that csstype's Property.Color pulls in.
  • Color functions are configurable too. They now default to honey-style's resolveColor alone - getColor and getContrastColor are not honey-style API. Add them back, or add your own wrappers, in settings.

0.3.1

  • Plain CSS colors get a swatch where honey resolves one - $backgroundColor="white" and resolveColor('#318BFA'). Picking a color there writes a hex value rather than snapping to a theme token.

0.3.0

  • Honey-layout color props are supported: $backgroundColor="accent.mediumGold" gets a swatch, Cmd/Ctrl+Click and completion. JSX props parse to XML rather than JS PSI, so they were previously skipped.
  • Only the props honey-layout actually resolves a path for are handled - $color, $backgroundColor, $borderColor and the four per-side variants, $outlineColor, $textDecorationColor, $fill, $stroke. Other props pass the string through unchanged, so a path there would emit invalid CSS.

0.2.0

  • The deprecated colors2 object is no longer indexed - it collided with colors on paths such as secondary.light, where the two hold different values.
  • A path inside a template literal is no longer claimed by both the color provider and the line marker provider.
  • Template color markers are mergeable, matching the platform's own color markers.

0.1.0

  • Gutter color swatches for honey-style theme color paths, with a picker that snaps to the nearest palette token.
  • Cmd/Ctrl+Click on a color path jumps to the declaration holding the value.
  • Color path completion, with the color shown as the item icon.
  • @honey-* at-rule completion inside styled/css template literals, with parameters and quick documentation. @honey-media breakpoints are read from the project's theme.breakpoints.
